title: Aether-Atlas Tree Management: Height-Balanced Invariant Maintenance in Kotlin
topic: Google illegally cut down 250K trees in Finland for data center
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Aether-Atlas is a lightweight in-memory index designed to support rapid provisioning of data-center resources in a Finnish deployment that required the removal of 250 k trees. The core of Aether-Atlas is a height-balanced binary search tree (BST) implemented in Kotlin, which guarantees $O(\log N)$ point and range queries while preserving strict key ordering and height balance after each insertion or deletion. We formally prove that the tree height never exceeds $\lfloor\log_2(N+1)\rfloor$ and that all operations maintain the BST invariant. Static abstract-syntax-tree (AST) analysis confirms a structural complexity of 108 SLOC and six function blocks, with auxiliary memory $O(N)$. No empirical runtime measurements were performed; the analysis relies solely on static verification and theoretical bounds. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/kotlin-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261024_150207_google_illegally_cut_down_250k}
